assumptions: Only Cinder earned XP scales; observed kills, movement, pressure, loot and consumable costs remain fixed.
Engine rounds XP separately per kill. These linear projections cannot recover exact rounding without a new run.
The benchmark freezes level and permanent mastery. Real progression speed can change how long a human stays in a map.
Map-wide scalar also applies to ordinary kills in Cinder optional circuit; its own optional-to-main ratio therefore stays approximately unchanged.
Before means reconstructed old authoring on the same corrected engine. It is not an old engine build.

recommendation.rationale: A conservative seven-percent correction lowers mean distance outside the target bands by 30.8%, reduces XP failures from 31 to 28, preserves a substantial improvement over before authoring, and introduces no deep-field premium above25%. It does not solve remaining class-specific encounter deficits.
tradeoffs: L28 Bandit and Quarry party premiums rise from 13.0%/15.9% to 21.5%/24.6%, creating two modest target misses.
L19 Archer ordinary deviation projects to 15.017%, still strictly outside 15%; the value must not be rounded into a pass.
The 151-point diagnostic grid chooses 0.928 under the no-new-above25 guard, but 0.93 avoids tuning to a three-seed threshold with spurious precision.
Exact runtime per-kill rounding and optional XP still require observed reruns if adopted.
